To me, the "Fallen Angel" music video seems to reveal Jennie's most vulnerable and human side. A fallen angel symbolizes someone who, despite appearing strong and having everything on the outside, can feel lost and lonely on the inside.

The wings represent freedom and dreams, while the image of a "fallen angel" represents the difficult moments, wounds, and entire journey she underwent to reach her current position.

This music video conveys the message that it is okay to get lost sometimes. It suggests that even if you stumble and undergo changes multiple times, you can continue moving forward and find your own place. It is a work that beautifully showcases Jennie's more personal and vulnerable side.

Hi Jennie and BLINKs! 💗 My name is Nadim, I'm a 20-year-old boy from India, and I've been a BLINK for 5 years.

I'm single, and I don't have a girlfriend or close friends. Sometimes, when I see other people with their partners and best friends, I feel a little lonely. But in my heart, I feel like I have four special girls who bring happiness and comfort into my life Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, and Lisa. 🥹🖤💗

I love these four girls so much, and I will always support them. Every morning when I wake up, one of the first things I do is look at their beautiful faces because they bring me peace, happiness, and a smile. Somehow, they've found a special place deep in my heart that words can never fully explain. ❤️

My biggest dream is to meet Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, and Lisa in person at least once in my life. I don't know if that dream will ever come true, but I'll never stop hoping. No matter how much time passes, I'll never forget them or the happiness they've brought into my life.

They may never know that someone like me exists, and they may never read this comment, but I still want to express my feelings. They aren't just my favourite idols; they're a very special part of my life. I'll keep cheering for them and loving their music for years to come. 🖤💗

제니, 어디서부터 시작해야 할지도 모르겠어요… 🥹🖤
저는 우즈베키스탄에 살고 있는 12살 팬이에요. 그리고 제가 제니의 팬이 된 지 벌써 4년이 되었어요.
제가 8살이었을 때 제니를 알게 되었고, 그때부터 지금까지 제니를 계속 사랑하고 응원해 왔어요. 🥹
4년이라는 시간 동안 제 삶에는 정말 많은 것들이 변했고, 저도 많이 변했어요. 하지만 변하지 않은 것 중 하나는 제니를 향한 제 마음이에요.
아마 제니는 저를 절대 모르겠죠. 수많은 댓글 중에서 이 댓글을 보지 못할 수도 있어요. 그래도 꼭 쓰고 싶었어요. 마음속에 있는 감정들을 계속 간직하고만 있기에는 너무 벅차서요. 😭
제니는 제 삶에 단순히 유명한 사람으로 들어온 게 아니에요. 제니의 노래, 목소리, 웃는 모습, 무대 위에서의 모습, 그리고 그냥 작은 미소 하나까지도 저에게는 정말 많은 추억과 연결되어 있어요.
기분이 좋지 않았던 날들도 있었고, 아무에게도 이야기하고 싶지 않았던 순간들도 있었어요. 그럴 때 제니를 보고 제니의 노래를 들으면, 적어도 조금이라도 마음이 편해지고 괜찮아질 수 있었어요.
제니는 모르겠죠… 그리고 저는 제니가 꼭 알아주기를 바라지도 않아요. 그저 한 가지만 말하고 싶어요.
제니가 하고 있는 일이 누군가의 삶에 정말 큰 의미가 될 수 있다는 것. 그리고 저에게는 정말 큰 의미라는 것. 🥹
저는 제니를 무대 위의 제니뿐만 아니라, 열심히 노력하고 꿈을 꾸고, 때로는 지치기도 하지만 그래도 계속 앞으로 나아가는 한 사람으로서도 정말 소중하게 생각해요.
4년 동안 제니를 지켜보면서 저도 제 자신을 조금 더 믿는 법을 배웠고, 꿈을 포기하지 않는 법과 있는 그대로의 나 자신이 되는 것을 두려워하지 않는 법을 배웠어요.
제니에게 완벽해지라고 말하고 싶지는 않아요. 제니는 지금 그대로의 모습만으로도 충분히 소중한 사람이니까요. 다만 제발 제니 자신을 잘 돌봐줬으면 좋겠어요.
사람들은 제니에게 정말 많은 것을 기대할 수도 있지만, 제니도 행복할 권리가 있고, 쉴 권리가 있고, 그냥 한 사람의 ‘제니’로 편안하게 살아갈 권리가 있으니까요. 🖤
언젠가 제가 제니를 직접 만날 수 있는 날이 온다면, 아마 너무 긴장해서 무슨 말을 해야 할지 몰라 아무 말도 못 할 것 같아요. 어쩌면 그냥 울어버릴지도 몰라요. 😭
우즈베키스탄에서 4년 동안 화면 너머로 제니를 사랑하고 응원해 온 제가, 언젠가 정말 눈앞에서 제니를 볼 수 있다면 그 순간은 제 인생에서 절대 잊지 못할 순간이 될 것 같아요.
제니, 제니는 저를 모르지만 저는 제니에게 정말 감사해요.
제 인생의 가장 예쁜 추억들 중 일부에는 제니의 노래가 함께하고 있어요. 어떤 날들에는 제니의 미소가 함께했고, 제 꿈들 중에는 제니에게서 받은 영감이 담겨 있어요.
4년이 지났지만 저는 여전히 여기 있어요.
여전히 제니를 응원하고, 여전히 제니를 자랑스러워하고, 여전히 제니를 알게 된 것에 감사하고 있어요. 🖤
“사랑해요”라는 말을 아무리 많이 해도 제 마음속에 있는 모든 감정을 다 표현하기에는 부족한 것 같아요.
그저… 존재해줘서 고마워요, 제니.
제니는 저를 모르겠지만, 제 마음속 가장 예쁜 곳 중 하나에는 항상 제니의 이름이 있을 거예요. 🥹🖤
저는 우즈베키스탄에서 제니를 응원하고 있는 12살 팬이에요.
언젠가 제니가 이 댓글을 보게 된다면, 멀리 우즈베키스탄에도 제니를 진심으로 사랑하고 응원하는 팬이 있다는 것만 기억해 줬으면 좋겠어요. 🇺🇿🖤

I honestly think people are looking way too deeply into the dark imagery and not enough into the actual lyrics. If you simply read the song, the meaning is pretty understandable. “Fallen angel” doesn’t automatically mean something demonic or related to the Illuminati. It can represent someone who feels lost, vulnerable, or like they’ve fallen away from where they belong. The whole song keeps coming back to not wanting to be left alone, searching for someone, and wanting to find a place that can become a home. Even the line about her wings being useless without someone shows that the “angel” imagery is being used emotionally, not literally. I think some people just aren’t used to seeing Jennie in this kind of vulnerable and melancholic concept, so they focus more on the visuals and immediately assume the worst instead of trying to understand what the song is actually saying. You don’t have to like the song or the MV, but calling it demonic just because it uses dark angel imagery feels like missing the point of the song itself.

하나님의 성결과 위엄: 거룩하고 순결하신 성부 하나님의 속성을 상징합니다.

Jennie’s "Fallen Angel" (Real Meaning):The Theme: It's a purely artistic song about emotional dependency and growth. It has absolutely nothing to do with spirits, demons, or rituals.The Fallen Angel: A metaphor for vulnerability. The line "without you, these wings mean nothing" shows that success or freedom matters little when feeling lonely.Fire & Thorns: They do not represent evil. In art, fire symbolizes purifying and burning past traumas, while thorns represent life's hardships.The Message: Life's struggles (thorns) are what make us evolve and bloom into the "most beautiful roses." It is a story of personal healing.

"Fallen Angel" da Jennie: O Significado RealO Tema Central: É uma história puramente artística sobre dependência emocional e superação, sem nada a ver com espíritos, rituais ou demônios.O Anjo Caído: É apenas uma metáfora para a vulnerabilidade. A frase "sem você, essas asas não servem para nada" mostra que o sucesso não importa se ela estiver se sentindo sozinha.O Fogo e os Espinhos: Não representam o "mal" ou o inferno. Na arte, o fogo simboliza purificação (queimar os traumas do passado) e os espinhos são as dificuldades da vida.A Mensagem Final: O clipe encerra mostrando que, embora o caminho seja difícil, são as superações que fazem as "rosas mais bonitas" desabrocharem. É sobre evolução pessoal.

Bíblicamente, los ángeles son seres espirituales creados por Dios antes del mundo físico para adorarlo, obedecer su voluntad y actuar como mensajeros suyos.

¿Qué significan y cómo son?

El nombre: La palabra ángel viene del griego ángelos y del hebreo malák, que significan exactamente "mensajero". 

Naturaleza espiritual: No tienen un cuerpo físico como los humanos, sino que son espíritus. Sin embargo, la Biblia muestra que pueden tomar forma humana visible cuando es necesario. 

Personalidad: Tienen inteligencia, emociones y la capacidad de decidir. La Biblia señala que la mayoría permanece obediente a Dios, pero un grupo se rebeló y se convirtió en demonios. 

Poder: Son mucho más fuertes e inteligentes que los seres humanos, aunque su conocimiento y poder siguen siendo limitados comparados con los de Dios. 

¿Cuál es su función?

Llevar mensajes: Anuncian planes divinos importantes, como ocurrió con el ángel Gabriel al hablar con María o Zacarías.

Proteger y guiar: Cuidan de los fieles en momentos de peligro o necesidad por mandato de Dios.

Alabar a Dios: Pasan su tiempo en el cielo glorificando al Creador sin descanso.

Ejecutar justicia: Actúan como instrumentos del juicio de Dios contra el mal.

Buenas, Dios los bendiga 😉

Los seres humanos son criaturas especiales creadas a imagen y semejanza de Dios, compuestas por un cuerpo físico y un componente espiritual. 

Creación y Naturaleza

A imagen de Dios: Los humanos reflejan las cualidades de Dios, como el amor, la justicia y la creatividad.

Origen dual: Dios formó el cuerpo físico del ser humano con el polvo de la tierra y sopló en él aliento de vida.

Tres dimensiones: La Biblia describe al ser humano integrado por espíritu, alma y cuerpo. El cuerpo conecta con el mundo físico, el alma comprende la mente y las emociones, y el espíritu permite la relación con Dios. 

Propósito y Rol

Mayordomía: Recibieron la autoridad y la tarea de cuidar, administrar y gobernar la creación de Dios de forma responsable.

Naturaleza relacional: Fueron diseñados para vivir en comunidad, relacionándose tanto con su Creador como con los demás seres humanos.

La caída del ser humano bíblicamente es el momento en que Adán y Eva desobedecieron a Dios en el Jardín del Edén, lo que introdujo el pecado y la muerte al mundo. Este relato se encuentra en el libro de Génesis, capítulo 3. 

El Relato en el Edén 

El mandato: Dios puso a Adán y Eva en un lugar perfecto y les dio libertad de comer de todo, excepto del árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal.

La tentación: Una serpiente (asociada con Satanás) engañó a Eva al dudar de la palabra de Dios y sugerir que serían como Dios.

La desobediencia: Eva y Adán comieron el fruto prohibido de forma deliberada. 

Consecuencias Principales 

Ruptura espiritual: Se rompió la comunión directa y cercana que los humanos tenían con Dios, sintiendo vergüenza y culpa. 

Entrada del sufrimiento y la muerte: La maldición trajo dolor en el trabajo, dificultad en la crianza/parto y la mortalidad física para toda la humanidad. 

Naturaleza pecaminosa: Este acto afectó a toda la descendencia, heredando una tendencia hacia el pecado.  La naturaleza humana queda corrompida y afectada por una inclinación hacia el mal

La Promesa de Restauración

A pesar del castigo y la expulsión del Edén, la Biblia plantea desde ese mismo momento un plan divino de redención a través de Jesucristo para reconciliar a la humanidad con Dios. Todo esto lo dice la biblia 🙂‍↕️

El plan divino de salvación en Jesucristo es la iniciativa de Dios para rescatar a la humanidad del pecado y ofrecerle vida eterna a través del sacrificio y la resurrección de su Hijo. 


Este plan se compone de etapas esenciales:

Las Etapas del Plan de Salvación 

La creación y el propósito: Dios creó al mundo y al ser humano en perfecta armonía, con el propósito de tener una relación cercana con él.

El problema del pecado: La humanidad se apartó de Dios mediante la desobediencia, introduciendo el pecado al mundo. Esto creó una separación entre Dios y el ser humano, cuya consecuencia es la muerte espiritual. 

La provisión en Jesucristo: Como las personas no pueden salvarse por sí mismas, Dios envió a Jesucristo. Jesús vivió sin pecado y pagó el precio de las faltas humanas al morir en la cruz.

La respuesta humana: La salvación se recibe por gracia mediante la fe en Jesucristo, el arrepentimiento sincero de los pecados y la aceptación de su sacrificio redentor. 

La restauración final: El plan culmina con la promesa de la vida eterna y la restauración plena de la comunión con Dios. 😊

What does fallen angel mean?
The fallen angel is Jennie’s metaphor for someone who feels lost and Direction less when a person they deeply care about isn’t there anymore. Normally, an angel has wings so they can go anywhere, but in the song, the idea is basically” What is the point of having wings if I don’t have you to fly toward “ she is searching for this person, asking them to stay and imagining that wherever they end up together could become home from home isn’t really a house or a country home is the person. And that makes the title clear She isn’t necessary of fallen angel because she did something wrong. She’s fallen angel because she has wings, but no direction, and she feels abandoned on her own. There is also slightly deeper interpretation that I actually find interesting Her love is becoming too dependent. She basically treats this person as the thing that gives her wings meaning. One analysis reads the song as someone who still has the ability to fly independently, but doesn’t realise it because she is so focused on getting another person to stay.

It is a truly beautiful video and a beautiful song.
But the story in this video has scenes that remind me of the horror films “INSIDIOUS” and “MIDSOMMAR.” (and “Illuminati”)

In particular, the burning house at the end reminds me of the house that burned with the man wearing the bear skin in MIDSOMMAR.
The red veils worn by the young girls look as if they are stained with blood, and they bring to mind baby angels with their heads cut off.

The child inside the burning house, surrounded by flames, is speaking as if she is about to cry, with a terrified, tearful expression.
Jennie closing their eyes with her own hands feels almost like it symbolizes human sacrifice and being reborn through it.

(But in reality, what Jennie probably intended was to personify both the young girls and Jennie herself as red roses that overcame pain and bloomed beautifully.)

There may be many positive meanings in this music video, but when you watch the visuals without thinking too deeply, that is how it feels.
Whatever Jennie intended, many people seem to feel the same way I do.

In Korea, there are countless reactions saying that this music video is extremely bizarre and frightening because it evokes the horror films INSIDIOUS and MIDSOMMAR, and seems to use the motif of child human sacrifice.

I think this song is about the wounds she carried from her childhood.
She sees herself as a fallen angel, perhaps because she never felt like the beloved child in her family.
She begged her mother to stay with her, but in the end she was left behind in New Zealand at the age of nine. She once spoke in an interview about the psychological trauma of having to move to New Zealand alone.
She grew up lonely, looking out the window at other families who had each other, while she had no one but herself and the blue roses her mother gave her on every birthday.
She longed for love, but to her it felt like a flickering light, because that hope was so fragile. The only moments of freedom and peace came when she could escape the cramped house, with its television endlessly broadcasting a toxic entertainment world. Yet whenever the New Year arrived, the brilliant fireworks would pull her back into feelings of isolation and sorrow.
There was never truly a place she could call home, and perhaps the same was true for her mother. As she grew older, she came to understand that the sharpest thorns, the ones that hurt her the most, were also what helped her become one of the most beautiful roses in the world. She has made peace with that now and wants the lonely, wounded child inside her to finally rest.
More than anything, she wished she could run away with her mother to a place they could call home. Perhaps she has finally achieved that now. Mother and daughter are living together at last.

I love that girl so much. ❤

Explanation: of ending part

Jennie is led by a young child wearing angel wings and holding a candle to a structure entirely engulfed in flames. Jennie walks into the fire with ease, symbolizing a willingness to confront her deepest anxieties, painful memories, or the intense pressure of her public life. Inside the burning structure, she finds an identical younger counterpart (her inner child). Both are dressed in red, trapped inside a cocoon or nest made of sharp, protective thorns

While trapped in the thorns, the younger girl delivers a poignant spoken-word line to adult Jennie 
                          Lyrics: Thorns may be the sharpest, fiercest thing on this earth. And yet, they bloom into the world's most beautiful roses 

This dialogue recontextualizes the video's earlier imagery of frozen blue roses. The "thorns" represent the defense mechanisms, isolation, and hardships she had to build up to survive global stardom. The ending suggests that pain and vulnerability aren't just destructive—they are necessary catalysts for growth and beautiful transformation

As a haunting children's choir rises in the background, Jennie looks directly forward and reaches out to place her hand over the camera lens, effectively closing the viewers' eyes. This final gesture acts as a boundary. By cutting off the viewer, Jennie reclaims her privacy and signals that while she is willing to share her vulnerability through her art, her true internal self belongs only to her

This MV feels like a whole story about a fallen angel searching for love, freedom, and a place to belong. 🪽 At first, Jennie feels almost trapped in this beautiful fantasy world, surrounded by all these angelic and fairytale-like images, but underneath all the beauty there’s so much loneliness. The little girl with the wings feels like an important part of her journey, almost like the innocent side of herself that is still looking for somewhere safe to belong.

The scenes with the swans, the lake, the forest, the house, and Jennie underwater all feel like different parts of this dreamlike journey. It feels like she's slowly confronting things she has been trying to escape from. The water almost feels like she's being pulled deeper into her own emotions, while the angel imagery shows that even something that looks beautiful and perfect can still feel lost.

Then we see the couples and all the imagery surrounding love, which makes the lyrics hit even harder. She's surrounded by love but still feels alone, and that's what makes her “fall” feel less like becoming evil and more like losing the feeling of having somewhere to belong.

And the ending with the little girl, the burning house, and Jennie becoming surrounded by thorns is so heartbreaking. 🔥🌹 It feels like she finally stops running from everything and faces it. The thorns are painful, but they can also become roses, so maybe the pain and loneliness she's experienced are part of what allows her to become her true self.

I don't think the fallen angel is someone who needs to return to heaven. I think she's someone who had to fall in order to discover who she really is. And in the end, she finds freedom not by becoming perfect again, but by accepting herself. 🪽🌹

FALLEN ANGEL is essentially a story about love, temptation, losing yourself in someone, and eventually recognizing that the relationship isn't what you imagined it to be.
The “fallen angel” idea works as a metaphor: Jennie presents someone who initially seems almost pure, beautiful, or heavenly, but gets pulled into something complicated and emotionally destructive.
The storyline can be understood in a few stages:
1. ✨ The angelic beginning
At first, there's an almost dreamlike attraction. Everything feels beautiful and special, as though the other person is someone worth completely surrendering yourself to.
2. 🖤 Falling
The “fall” represents becoming emotionally attached and losing some of your independence. The relationship becomes increasingly complicated, with desire and vulnerability mixed together.
3. 🌑 Reality sets in
Eventually, the fantasy doesn't match reality. The person or relationship that seemed perfect has darker sides. The angel isn't simply “evil”—she's hurt, conflicted, and changed by what she's experienced.
4. 🪽 Becoming your own person
The important part is that being a “fallen angel” doesn't necessarily mean being ruined forever. It's more like falling from an idealized version of love and seeing things clearly.
So, rather than a literal story about an angel falling from heaven, it's better interpreted as an emotional metaphor for falling hard for someone and discovering the complicated reality behind that love.

The wings represent freedom and dreams, while the image of a "fallen angel" represents the difficult moments, wounds, and entire journey she underwent to reach her current position.

This music video conveys the message that it is okay to get lost sometimes. It suggests that even if you stumble and undergo changes multiple times, you can continue moving forward and find your own place. It is a work that beautifully showcases Jennie's more personal and vulnerable side.

Watching the video for the second time made me think and interpret the whole song in a way that this is Jennie’s lament to her father.

The first part of the video where the girl says they can still fly and be free as can be makes me think that it is her mom talking to her, assuring her that they can still be happy without him. And seeing all the kids in this music video outside of a house burning down makes me think of kids without a home or without their parents present in their lives: fallen angels, but not in the biblical sense.

“Hey, can’t you stay?” Sounds like a desperate plea coming from a kid who sees her parent one foot out the door.

And all the frozen blue roses are what keeps Jennie’s home from burning down. Mama Kim ALWAYS gives Jennie blue roses for her birthday.

And the geese! They appeared many times. Geese symbolise teamwork, loyalty, and vigilance to protect their young, yet they always appear alone (the stuffed toy, and the shadow by the window) or moving away from each other (0:48) … They were watching Jennie floating, but they didn’t catch her! Geese fly in a V formation to share the workload and help weaker members travel further. In this MV, they did opposite of what they represent. And it’s just BRILLIANT!

The MV also evokes an uneasy/scary feeling right after the song ends, maybe it is to make us feel how scary the world is for kids without a home/family.

The last monologue breaks my heart… it appears to me that little Jennie is comforting the older Jennie. It seemed like she was considered a “thorn” when she was younger, yet her she is now, the world’s most beautiful flower.

Jennie has the mind of a great storyteller and sunburnkids did it justice.

PS. These are all my point of view/interpretation. You’re welcome to have a different view and scroll down.

어떤 모습이든, 어디에 있든, 저는 언제나 제니, 지수, 로제, 리사를 응원할 거예요. 그리고 앞으로도 영원히 BLINK인 것이 자랑스러울 거예요. 🖤💖

우리의 네 명, 그리고 BLACKPINK를 언제나 사랑해요. 영원히 함께해요. ♾️🖤💗

this music video is so beautifully made, but here are some details i’ve noticed. 

num 1: A child with all eyes on her anticipating what her next move is and judging her, kinda like the young girls in the entertainment industry.

num 2: Jennie floating, and the swans (seem innocent) looking up to her, [maybe young girls idolizing her] and jennie in her white outfit signifying her innocence to the world. 

num 3: After Jennie makes a single motion with her legs or arms all the swans leave. Jennie is then on the ground under the storm and remembers how hard the hit was when she fell to the ground and the impact it left in her.

Num 4: She is no longer bathe in her innocent view of the world but now covered in red. Either a metaphor of her innocent view of the world being completely tarnished and turned red like a wound, or because she was badly wounded she carries her trauma with pride and continues about her career.

Num 5: the hole is perhaps her last chance of hope and freedom to be herself and the fear of breaking that wall and reliving everything that happened in her innocence scares her but she breaks the wall anyways and runs innocently with butterflies and is happy, she keeps running innocently without realizing she runs back to the same room she tried leaving and falls again like in the beginning—Only this time there is noise and fireworks but she is still in pain but decides to stay for a while. Perhaps this is her way of expressing how every move she does comes with outrage from the media and yet people applaud her and pay money to watch her perform whether she is in pain, happy, or at her worst. but it still hurts her and she does it alone, yet she gets up and keeps on going.

This music video conveys the message that it is okay to get lost sometimes. It suggests that even if you stumble and undergo changes multiple times, you can continue moving forward and find your own place. It is a work that beautifully showcases Jennie's more personal and vulnerable side.

Girl chill, there’s nothing scary. The fallen angel (and thus the beginning) represents the feeling of being lost, alone, and wounded. It clearly conveys that a fallen angel should not be left alone, expressing a sense of abandonment. She seeks a place of refuge to call home. The little girl who appears represents her inner child. Jennie’s gesture of closing her eyes symbolizes shutting out the expectations of others (the little girl’s brief monologue speaks of greed—specifically, how the world’s selfishness and material possessions weigh people down, preventing them from flying). Jennie tells us that even after falling and getting hurt, it is possible to regain one’s freedom and fly. The monologue is very clear: “But my little one, close your eyes like I do. We can still fly. Bananas are technically berries, while strawberries are not. Botanically speaking, a berry is a fruit that develops from a single ovary of a flower and contains seeds embedded within the flesh, which is exactly how bananas form. Each banana develops from a flower with a single ovary, and the tiny black specks you sometimes see inside are the remnants of seeds. Strawberries, on the other hand, are considered “aggregate fruits” because they develop from multiple ovaries of a single flower, with each little seed-like speck (called an achene) on the outside being its own tiny fruit. Interestingly, this botanical definition of berries means that other fruits you wouldn’t expect—like kiwis, grapes, and even tomatoes—fit the true definition of a berry, while many of the fruits we commonly call berries, like raspberries and blackberries, technically don’t.

After watching “Fallen Angel,” I felt like something inside me quietly broke open. I thought I was only listening to a song, but somehow it felt like I was stepping into an emotion I couldn’t escape. I couldn’t even watch it fully because every second felt heavier than the last. The voice, the eyes, the lyrics, and the silence between the moments felt like they were speaking directly to a hidden part of my heart.

I don’t know why, but I became afraid. My heart felt heavy, my hands trembled, and I felt lost inside a feeling I couldn’t name. It was like sadness and beauty were standing together in the same place. I wanted to look away because it hurt, but at the same time, I couldn’t let go.

The song felt like a memory I never lived, a goodbye I never said, and a pain I never knew I carried. It made me feel lonely in a way I couldn’t explain like I was holding a thousand emotions inside but had no words to release them.

But why does a song have the power to make us feel this way? Why can a voice, a melody, or a story reach so deeply into our hearts and bring out emotions we never knew existed? Why do some moments stay with us, even after the music stops? I still don’t know the answer, but maybe that is what makes certain songs unforgettable.

I don’t even know where to start… today your new ep, ‘fallen angel’, came out, which I had really been waiting for for such a long time. People won’t understand what I’m feeling right now, how much I’ve been waiting for its release and how much all of this means to me.
fallen angel for me is not a single song, it’s not simply an ep. For me it is tranquility, it is that little place where I manage to feel good, that little moment where I stop thinking about all those thoughts I have in my head, and simply let myself be carried away by your beautiful, delicate voice, even if I only feel this for a few minutes. When I open spotify, the first thing I think about is typing your name into the search bar, and listening to your songs. It has almost become a habit, one of those little things that may seem insignificant, but that mean so much to me. Because I know that, whatever kind of day I’m having, somehow in your songs I always manage to find something I needed, in your songs I manage to find myself again. It rarely happens that I manage to become attached to something, to people, but you managed to do it, and this means so much to me. I know you will never know me in your life, but I want to remind you of the special person you are inside, even though I don’t know what happens in your life outside of this. And it happens even more rarely that I can find words that are able to describe what I feel. And maybe that’s exactly why fallen angel feels so special to me, because I’m not simply listening to it, I’m living it. I don’t know if I’ll ever be able to truly explain to you how much your music means to me. Probably no sentence will ever be enough to describe the effects you have on me, but I hope you can know that, on the other side, there is someone who listens to every song of yours with their heart, who waits for every project of yours with a happiness that is impossible to explain, and who today is simply happy to finally have fallen angel with them. Watching the MV, I had the feeling of entering your world for a few minutes, into the story you wanted to tell, and I didn’t want time to pass. I’ve been waiting for all of this since you first spoiled ‘lock it down’.
I really don’t know how to explain how stunning it is. The plot, the way you decided to tell it, every scene, every detail… everything seems to have an emotional meaning. It’s one of those videos that you can’t simply watch and nothing more, because while you’re watching it, you feel something inside and you keep wondering what is behind every single scene. The MV hides something deep and emotional inside, a feeling that is perhaps mysterious, something you feel but don’t say. I was so struck by the way you managed to turn the meaning of the fallen angel into images. The story of the angel, her fall, everything she goes through… it’s as if every scene tells a part of those emotions that maybe cannot even be explained with words. And the more I watch it, the more I realize how carefully every little detail was made.
I think the most beautiful thing about the MV is that it doesn’t simply give you a story to watch from the outside, but a story that you feel inside yourself, and in such a short amount of time it manages to leave you with a message. I don’t know how many times I’ll watch it again, probably so many, but I already know that every time I’ll find something different and manage to feel something new, like the first time I saw it. I’ve been waiting for this all summer, or maybe even before, but I’m proud of it. Thank you for creating something that manages to make me feel so much. Thank you for putting a part of yourself into these songs and for allowing us to make them, in some way, a little bit ours too. 🩵🪽

I don’t even know where to start… today your new ep, ‘fallen angel’, came out, which I had really been waiting for for such a long time. People won’t understand what I’m feeling right now, how much I’ve been waiting for its release and how much all of this means to me.
fallen angel for me is not a single song, it’s not simply an ep. For me it is tranquility, it is that little place where I manage to feel good, that little moment where I stop thinking about all those thoughts I have in my head, and simply let myself be carried away by your beautiful, delicate voice, even if I only feel this for a few minutes. When I open spotify, the first thing I think about is typing your name into the search bar, and listening to your songs. It has almost become a habit, one of those little things that may seem insignificant, but that mean so much to me. Because I know that, whatever kind of day I’m having, somehow in your songs I always manage to find something I needed, in your songs I manage to find myself again. It rarely happens that I manage to become attached to something, to people, but you managed to do it, and this means so much to me. I know you will never know me in your life, but I want to remind you of the special person you are inside, even though I don’t know what happens in your life outside of this. And it happens even more rarely that I can find words that are able to describe what I feel. And maybe that’s exactly why fallen angel feels so special to me, because I’m not simply listening to it, I’m living it. I don’t know if I’ll ever be able to truly explain to you how much your music means to me. Probably no sentence will ever be enough to describe the effects you have on me, but I hope you can know that, on the other side, there is someone who listens to every song of yours with their heart, who waits for every project of yours with a happiness that is impossible to explain, and who today is simply happy to finally have fallen angel with them. Watching the MV, I had the feeling of entering your world for a few minutes, into the story you wanted to tell, and I didn’t want time to pass. I’ve been waiting for all of this since you first spoiled ‘lock it down’.
I really don’t know how to explain how stunning it is. The plot, the way you decided to tell it, every scene, every detail… everything seems to have an emotional meaning. It’s one of those videos that you can’t simply watch and nothing more, because while you’re watching it, you feel something inside and you keep wondering what is behind every single scene. The MV hides something deep and emotional inside, a feeling that is perhaps mysterious, something you feel but don’t say. I was so struck by the way you managed to turn the meaning of the fallen angel into images. The story of the angel, her fall, everything she goes through… it’s as if every scene tells a part of those emotions that maybe cannot even be explained with words. And the more I watch it, the more I realize how carefully every little detail was made.
I think the most beautiful thing about the MV is that it doesn’t simply give you a story to watch from the outside, but a story that you feel inside yourself, and in such a short amount of time it manages to leave you with a message. I don’t know how many times I’ll watch it again, probably so many, but I already know that every time I’ll find something different and manage to feel something new, like the first time I saw it. I’ve been waiting for this all summer, or maybe even before, but I’m proud of it. Thank you for creating something that manages to make me feel so much. Thank you for putting a part of yourself into these songs and for allowing us to make them, in some way, a little bit ours too. 🩵🪽
Thank you for what you do for us Jennie

🪽 Antes de juzgar el MV de FALLEN ANGEL, una pequeña explicación:

Sí, el video tiene una estética oscura, fuego y escenas fuertes, pero no es una historia sobre maldad ni sobre Jennie siendo una villana.

El MV representa un viaje de transformación: una persona que pierde parte de su inocencia, atraviesa el dolor, el amor y la soledad, y finalmente aprende a aceptar quién es.

👧 La niña representa la inocencia y la libertad.
🔥 El fuego representa dejar atrás y transformar una etapa.
🌹 Las espinas representan el dolor y las dificultades.
🦋 Las mariposas representan el cambio y la transformación.
🪽 El “ángel caído” representa a alguien que cayó, cambió y conoció el lado difícil de la vida, pero que sigue siendo él mismo.

Así que si entrás al MV y te sorprenden las imágenes oscuras, no te quedes solamente con lo visual. Hay una historia y un significado detrás de ellas.

En pocas palabras: es un MV sobre caer, sufrir, transformarse y aprender a aceptarse. 🖤🪽

~~ FALLEN ANGEL de JENNIE~~

Aunque el MV tiene una estética oscura, fuego y escenas que pueden parecer perturbadoras, la historia no trata simplemente de que Jennie sea “la villana”.

La niña representa la inocencia y esa parte de nosotros que todavía cree en la libertad y en los sueños. Jennie aparece como un ángel que ha caído y comienza un viaje por diferentes emociones: el amor, la soledad, la búsqueda de un hogar y el dolor.

Las flores y las mariposas representan transformación, mientras que las grietas muestran cómo aquello que parecía perfecto puede romperse.

El fuego simboliza la destrucción y, al mismo tiempo, la transformación: dejar atrás una versión anterior de uno mismo. Por eso es tan importante la escena en la que Jennie se encuentra con la niña dentro de la casa en llamas. Puede interpretarse como un encuentro con su propia inocencia, con su “niña interior”.

La rosa entre las espinas resume gran parte del mensaje: el dolor y las dificultades también pueden formar parte de nuestro crecimiento y de aquello en lo que nos convertimos. 🌹

Por eso, ser un “fallen angel” no significa ser malo. Significa haber caído, haber conocido el lado difícil de la vida y haber cambiado sin dejar de ser uno mismo.

En resumen: no es una historia sobre una villana, sino sobre una caída, una transformación y la aceptación de uno mismo. 🪽🔥🌹

I’m a couple of hours late, but JENNIE just dropped another BANGER and an absolute masterpiece of a music video. 😭🪽🔥

JENNIE devoured every aspect of this performance and left NO crumbs. The heavenly vocals, songwriting, music, gorgeous visuals, cinematography, styling, acting chops, storytelling and EVERYTHING ELSE… she really did THAT.

I absolutely LOVE the concept and the fact that JENNIE and the entire creative team went for something so different with this dark fantasy, dark fairy-tale, dreamy, surreal and horror-inspired aesthetic. It’s beautiful and magical one moment, and then suddenly eerie, unsettling and creepy the next—and I LOVE that contrast. 🖤🌹

Some of the surreal visuals were also giving me a little bit of It’s Okay to Not Be Okay vibes. Not necessarily because I think JENNIE was directly inspired by the drama, but because of that similar combination of dark fairy-tale imagery, surrealism, fantasy, psychological darkness and horror. That drama also used surreal effects and different animation styles to tell its story, so I definitely felt that connection here.

And speaking of the horror influences, I could be completely wrong, but I feel like you can see and maybe even feel inspiration from both old-school and modern horror, dark fantasy and supernatural/apocalyptic stories throughout the video. The different animation and visual styles, the creepy imagery, the cult-like atmosphere and especially that ending really got my imagination going.

Because THAT ENDING??? 😭

There are so many ways to interpret it. JENNIE could be the angel, she could be the Fallen Angel, or it could represent a transformation of some kind.

But part of me wonders if there's an even darker interpretation:

What if JENNIE isn't just the Fallen Angel who has fallen from heaven… what if she's the Fallen Angel who has ARRIVED? 🪽🔥

The burning house, the unsettling atmosphere, the little girl leading someone toward it, the angelic imagery and then JENNIE sitting there so calmly before pointing directly at the camera…

It almost feels like something out of a supernatural horror or apocalypse story where a dark supernatural being arrives and is somehow connected to the end of the world.

I'm NOT saying that's officially what the video means—I could be completely off—but as a personal interpretation, I LOVE the possibility that the Fallen Angel could represent something much darker… maybe even the beginning of an Apocalypse. 🔥🪽

And I LOVE that the MV leaves enough ambiguity for us to interpret it in different ways instead of explaining everything to us.

The message of the music video is also so meaningful and beautiful. I was genuinely in awe and honestly a little emotional watching it. The acting from the entire cast was amazing, including the little girl, whom I’m assuming represents a younger JENNIE or some part of her inner self.

And that quote toward the end??? 😭🌹

It absolutely made me emotional because it's so beautiful and relatable.

Huge kudos to JENNIE, the director, and the entire creative team behind this song and music video. They created something that feels like a gorgeous, haunting, surreal dark fairy tale, and I am SO here for it.

And of course, JENNIE looked absolutely gorgeous and was styled beautifully, as always. 🥹😍🖤🩷🔴💎🪽

I cannot WAIT to listen to the entire EP digitally and physically because I already know this project is going to be in HEAVY ROTATION.

My interpretation of the mv

1. The Fall (Loss of Innocence): Plunging into the pond and losing her wings symbolizes hitting rock bottom under the pressure of fame and being stripped of her untouchable status.

2. The Red Dress (Rebirth & Freedom): Shattering the doorless room shows that her mental barriers were fragile. Walking on the ground represents finding peace in reality rather than trying to fly.

3. Faceless Crowds (Hollow Success): Navigating dark rooms with blurred people symbolizes the isolation of celebrity life, showing that the surrounding crowd does not truly care about her.

4. The Spotlight (City Loneliness): Turning her back under a bright city spotlight represents being hyper-visible to the world yet utterly alone and disconnected.

5. Three Pictures (Love Overcomes Everything): The photos of couples—on a sofa, young, and in prison—prove that genuine love brings warmth and happiness, no matter how trapped or damaged you are.

6. Burning House (Childhood Dream): The little angel represents her childhood dream of true love. The burning house signifies letting her old, artificial life burn away to build a real home from the ashes.

   Altogether, a good effort and a decent listen, but I do hope that the final version gets a re-mixed vocals line that takes out those effects and, if the guitar was intended to be like that, a re-recorded guitar that goes much harder on the fall.

okay now about the second half of the MV [JUST MY INTERPRETATION]

num 1: Jennie slides her hand in the water waving away this dystopian tale and the film turns monochrome which adds more definition to the music video. Kinda like skipping pages through a book only she’s turning the tale into a different time. 

Num 2: the fear of flying seems to be the overall theme here.

Num 3: The first couple we see shows a man who’s holding onto the woman and his art palette on the other hand. (kinda makes me think this is about two artists that are in love but split to follow their dreams). It seems like a reverse motion art— it’s shown to us that she pushes him away from the frame and then is left alone with a unfazed facial expression while the thin spotlight is on her. But when reversed— it shows us the man reaching out for a hug and she sees him and smiles and embraces him into a tight long lasting hug. 

Num 4: on the left to the first couple; frames of butterflies and another of an open field, and another of a man wearing a beret (possibly a military service uniform). It could quite literally mean she’s leaving them in the past, that’s why they’re on the left side bc they were “left” behind. The butterflies and field she ran through (the freedom she sacrificed for her own success and ability to fly on her own account, and maybe even left behind the idea of having a love life, a husband, a family, etc.) All these sacrifices left to be where she is now.

and to add to the first couple and the reason I believe Jennie turns the music video into monochrome is because we only see what’s in the light. But Jennie was there, she’s the only one who saw the whole thing because she herself is inside the frame, this is her life. We see only an ounce (hence the thin spotlight) but Jennie saw and lived what happened in the shadows and only she will carry that with her unless she brings us into that light. So the monochrome selection is a reality fact check that you can’t talk on a situation you know absolutely nothing about because nobody but herself knows what happened behind the scenes.

Next couple shows us more light, A man seems distressed and pleading to be forgiven and trying to buy her acceptance with roses of different shades but even though this man seems to be more economically stable— his flowers are not the best quality meaning this man isn’t what he seems but only she knows that through subtle hints in the shadows (that again only she knows of because she was there behind the scene and not us). The woman here also seems more economically stable, in a corvette perhaps and the same shades he has on but she takes them off and sees him for what he really is and rejects him. And the only glimpse we are left with is the woman’s face in the mirror. (Again we don’t see or understand what she had gone through or felt, we only see the actress (who i believe represents Jennie again) We only see what Jennie shows us when she makes a public appearance.

The third scene i don’t believe it’s a couple anymore. This i believe is Jennie’s way of sneaking in something very vulnerable about an experience with her and a Corporate Man or the man is representing ALL of the corporate industry. Again it’s a reversed motion depiction, It shows us a hesitant beautiful woman either an actress or singer who works under him but she’s outraged, went from being very close to confronting the man about an issue she has but then walks off and the Man smiles in the only light we see. In this version the woman (Jennie) comes off as someone who’s mean and aggressive in the light, and the man is just in the shadow 99% of the time until the end we just see a smiling man, kinda like how any controversial topic affects the artist but never the company. BUT when reversed it shows us what really happened, which was the woman (Jennie) storming in the office of the smiling man -who thinks he can get away with any scandal hidden in the shadows- to confront the man and she isn’t scared, she’s outrage about something and when she walks in the light it’s her way of letting him know she has something to say that she’s willing to bring into the light for everyone to see. In this version she doesn’t back out but walks closer to her face, she’s basically a threat.

the fourth scene : We finally see Jennie in the monochrome light but we don’t see who’s in the shadow, and she’s smiling then looks at us bothered. What I take from this is “you get it now? you knew nothing about me” because the media loves to judge and talk about her but never actually care to wait to hear her side of the story, we don’t know who else was involved and the overall TRUTH. and she walks away from our view. She then spins theatrically and the colors are back. Kinda like, “I will allow u into this part of my life”. She’s now in a new outfit kinda like 1920’s flapper style, She’s got jewels, she’s taking it all in.

Num 2: We see her in a foggy ice cube room of blue roses, blue curtains she’s near of, and one yellow light. 

Num 3: The blue roses I believe have personal ties to the roses her mother bought her for her birthday, but they’re frozen in time- the fog is either to keep them from dying out and protect this memory, or this happy memory is fading. Either way she takes a seat and wants to stay there, hold onto them, this is her safe space. And her looking out into the world and everyone else’s lives moving around her kinda tells us maybe this is the only thing keeping her sane in this chaotic place.

Unfortunately the beautiful Ice cube room of her mother’s blue roses turns dark, she’s forced to see herself in the mirror in the dark room with the only hint of reality is the yellow hotel light that doesn’t turn off. In that darkness this girl with a candle shows up and passes the candle onto her. The girl dressed in white with a red veil (most likely representing past young girls who were just as innocent and hurt by the industry and public eye at a young age passing this candle that ties them all together in the entertainment world.) 

And the story gets sadder after that. The woman who turned down the man with the poor quality roses is now trapped with the man and carries the candle and they both lower the glasses— aware of the real situation that they don’t belong together but stay together. The second couple decide to stay together most likely sacrificing both of their dreams and trapped in this relationship. As for the woman and corporate man, They carry the “torch” too both forcing themselves to smile with “Sill Love” in their teeth and anger/insanity in their eyes. I think this represents how Jennie -even after making her own label and success without YG still decided to signed another contract to stay with YG. She’s trapped, just like how many other young girls are trapped.  And then… the match that set fire to these candles blows out. We don’t know who lit it up but based off the nails lol I assume it was Jennie. And because Jennie has trapped herself, the little girl invites her to come with the rest of the other young “fallen angels” (because they’re not flying either). My interpretation is all these girls are either past and present young girls who sign under contracts to follow their dreams like Trainees and Idols, even models and actresses and dancers. The burning house is Jennie’s new home, this is her life now, and both her and her younger self are living this burden together to hold onto this dream of theirs.
